threads.title: Sai + Vermeil with Thrawn interaction on coordinate

posts.text:
When I run Thrawn on Vermeil and do the following:
Step 1: Sai coordinates Vermeil
Step 2: Vermeil uses the jam action
Step 3: Vermeil activates Thrawn for a coordinate
Step 4: Vermeil coordinates Sai
Step 5: Sai takes a focus through coordinate
Step 6: Sai jams through ability
Is this the correct order in the ability q for this interaction, because the coordinate from Sai hasn't finished yet before Thrawn activates?
What is the correct timing of all the triggers here? ("after action X you can do action Y" two of this triggers are present here, do they come at the same time and I can choose the timing or is there a certain order of it?)

posts.author: Hansi
posts.text:
Sai and Thrawn abilities trigger at the same time, the controlling player chooses the order to resolve the ability queue. This is the correct sequence:
• Sai coordinates Vermeil
• Vermeil performs a jam action
• Sai's ability triggers after the coordinated ship performed the action, Thrawn's one triggers at the same time
• controlling player chooses to resolve Thrawn first, so Vermeil coordinates Sai
• Sai performs a focus action granted by the coordinate from Vermeil
• controlling player now resolves Sai's ability to perfom a jam
Does the Mining Guild Tie skip its action step if it landed on an asteroid?

posts.author: Maui
posts.text:
No, the Mining Guild TIE does not skip its Perform Action step if it overlaps an asteroid.
Overlaps occur while a ship is moving. A maneuver is considered a type of move. When the Mining Guild TIE overlaps an obstacle, it is ignoring the obstacle with its Notched Stabilizers ability, so it does not suffer the effect of skipping its Perform Action step.

If Holo passes an enemy lock to a ship that is cloaked with sensor scramblers, is that ship a valid target? Does the lock transfer then break, or can the SS ship never take the transfer in the first place?

posts.author: Hansi
posts.text:
The solution to this interaction is similar to the one related to Amylin Holdo and self-locking defined in the FAQs of the RRG.
Holo can transfer the lock token to a friendly cloaked ship equipped with Sensor Scramblers, the token is removed from Holo and a new lock acquisition on the friendly ship is triggered but SS makes that ship a not valid target then the lock breaks.

If a Resistance ship carrying Amylin Holdo crew is locked by an enemy ship, and then uses Amylin Holdo to pass the lock token to a different friendly ship equipped with Ferrosphere Paint, assuming the Ferrosphere Paint ship is not in the bullseye arc of the ship that owns the lock token, does this trigger Ferrosphere Paint?

posts.author: Hansi
posts.text:
Yes, during the transfer the Lock token is removed from the ship carrying Holdo and it's assigned to the ship equipped with Ferrosphere Paint, so it gets locked by the enemy ship and Ferrosphere triggers.
Ferrosphere Paint got an errata to allow counterplay to this kind of interactions.

threads.title: Interloper Turn and Precision Ion Engine interaction

posts.text:
So... It's 4 in the morning here and sleeping is a problem, and it is rather beardy, but...
Interloper Turn
Before you execute a speed 1-2 turn or speed 1-2 Koiogran Turn, if you are at range 0-1 of an asteroid, structure, or huge ship, you may gain 1 tractor token
Precision Ion Engines
Before you execute a speed 1-3 Koiogran Turn maneuver, you may spend 1 Charge to execute that maneuver as a Segnor's Loop maneuver instead.
Can a TIE Defender reveal a 2 KTurn, perform an Interloper Tractor, then change the KTurn into a Sloop, OR are you forced to complete the KTurn if you Interloper Tractor first?
(I don't think that an argument can be made for doing Precision Ion Engines before Interloper... But let me know if that is incorrect too)
Both abilities state "Before you execute [a manoeuvre]", implying they both load into the queue at the player's timing of choice.
Both have the same trigger requirement of a KTurn, so as long as you have the KTurn set they both have a trigger at the times of declaring the ability to enter the queue and performing the ability...
So I am leaning towards Yes, you can Interloper Tractor before Precision Sloop, but I think that there is a discussion to be had.
And, I suppose thinking about that now, by extension, Ryad (with a 2 straight and with Ionisation 1 straights potentially turning into KTurns)? Would her ability alter this in any way?

posts.author: Maui
posts.text: Yes, this works. A TIE Defender with Interloper Turn and Precision Ion Engines can reveal a 2-Koiogran Turn and then choose to resolve Interloper Turn (gaining a tractor token) and then Precision Ion Engines (spending a charge to perform a Segnor's Loop instead of the K-turn).

Quick Build cards use Threat Value instead of standard squad building rules. They are not compatible with standard list building and they are not legal for tournament play.
For casual play, you can reference XWA points lists to estimate the costs of the cards involved.

The timing of the strain when a commando is deployed was brought into question during a match.
The card reads " After an enemy ship overlaps you, it gains 1 strain token."
The question that was asked said " An enemy ship has to move to overlap you, so deployment should not be causing an overlap"
I would like clarification on this as it has implications among other devices such as connor net and proxy mines. When a commando deploys, if it is placed under an enemy ship, does that ship gain a strain? Then after the commando moves, does the same ship gain another strain?
Mines also refer to the After a ship moves through or overlaps a ship, the mine triggers. This does trigger upon drop. I have always played and ruled this same trigger works with commando's.

posts.author: Hansi
posts.text:
The Overlap rules clearly explain how it works:
"After an object is placed, if it is placed underneath one or more ships, those ships resolve any effects of overlapping the object"
Commandos are objects so they follow this rule.
Can 311 pass 32C a Calc at the start of the engagement so that 32C can coordinate?

posts.author: Hansi
posts.text: DBS-32C cannot add its ability into the queue if it does not have any Calculate token at the start of the engagement phase. Abilities with a cost can be added into the queue only if the cost can be paid at the time of the trigger.

posts.text:
Two questions about Aurra’s pilot ability.
Can you transfer a token to one ship, then back to the original ship?
If you transfer a tractor token, reposition the ship, and the ship chooses to rotate, can you pass that new stress to the other ship?

posts.author: Hansi
posts.text: No, the transfer happens simultaneously. Once you choose the two ships, you also choose the tokens to be transferred and you exchange them between the ships at the same time.

A question came up tonight about how these two abilities interact together.
Chiss Engineering: After you fully execute a speed 3-5 maneuver, you may perform a Lock action. (...other part Irrelevant for this interaction)
Computer-Assisted Handling: After you fully execute a maneuver, you may spend 1 Charge to perform a Boost or Roll action.
One player using Captain Yorr executed a 3 Bank and loaded both abilities into the queue.
After performing Computer-Aided Handling Boost, that player then started to measure for Lock provided by Chiss Engineering for a target that was now in range but was highly unlikely to be before the Boost.
The disagreement was that the check for Lock should have been made when the ability went in the queue as that would be the point of "After you execute a manoeuvre".
The counterargument was that if you have abilities in the queue, you choose what order to execute them (such as in the Rules Reference pages 36-37 for Afterburners vs Fine-Tuned Controls).
The counter counterargument was that at the time of entering the queue the Lock would have been out of range and so would have been an invalid target, as per the "requirement for an ability" on page 36, and so another target must be chosen for the lock.
The counter counter counterargument was made that the Lock is an action so, just like the Afterburners/Fine-Tuned interaction, you choose when those actions take place and therefore when the checks take place.
We chose to allow the Boost before checking for Lock.
To summarise, the question is which of these (or other, if there is another option that we missed) is the correct resolution:
A
Both Chiss and Computer-Assist enter the queue, choose what happens first and execute that before testing the second.
OR
B
Both Chiss and Computer-Assist enter the queue, but you must check for Lock capabilities before executing either the Lock or Boost.

posts.author: Hansi
posts.text: The correct answer is the A, both upgrades are added to the queue and the player can choose the order to solve the abilities. Chiss Engineering doesn't have any requirement, so there is nothing to be satisfied to be added to the queue, except for the manoeuver speed.
If after i move, boost or perform BR, there is no enemy ship in my BE, do i still have to spend a charge?

posts.author: Hansi
posts.text: No, a ship can pay a cost for an effect only if the effect can be resolved, so you don't have to spend a charge if you cannot choose a ship in your bullseye.

cis durge is on 1 hp
gets 3hits
does he have to resolve his ability after the 1st dmg card?

posts.author: Hansi
posts.text:
It depends on the situation:
during an attack, Durge's ability resolves at the Aftermath step, after all damage cards have been dealt.
when damage is dealt by anything different from an attack, the ability is resolve after the first damage card. The remaining damage cards are dealt after the resolution of Durge's ability.
Seevor vs Qira: If a ship with Qira is overlapping an obstacle they have locked and they declare Seevor as the target, would Seevor ability, jamming off the lock, prevent the attack from happening?

posts.author: Hansi
posts.text:
No, Seevor's ability cannot prevent the attack because the ability triggers when the attack as already started. Seevor's triggers before rolling dice: once the lock is gone, the obstacle can obstruct the attack.
Seevor's ability can prevent the ship equipping Qira from performing a bonus attack after the first one.

threads.title: Echo SL interaction with eg Afterburner/retrofitted

posts.text: Does the ability from SL Echo work when somebody uses afterburners/retrofitted autothrusters and has the corresponding ability on their action bar?

posts.author: Maui
posts.text: Yes. As long as the action is on the ship's action bar, Echo's ability can resolve, even if the action was granted by another effect.

Savage Opress gives a focus when you gain stress or Strain.
Overtuned Modulators gives you a strain for left over Greens in the end phase.
So if you have a focus from that turn and you lose it at the end of the turn, and gain a strain from the Overtuned Modulators as it has no charge, Savage Opress can give that ship a focus. But can that ship keep the new focus from Savage Opress, as green tokens have already been removed?
Savage Opress "After a friendly ship in your Front Arc at range 1-2 gains a stress or strain token, you may spend 1 Force. If you do, that ship gains 1 focus token."
Overtuned Modulators "During the System Phase, if you are not stressed, you may spend 1 Charge to gain 3 calculate tokens.
During the End Phase, if your Charge is inactive, for each green token you remove, gain 1 strain token."
END PHASE
The End Phase is the fifth phase of the round. During the End Phase, the
following occur in this order:
• Abilities that occur "at the start of the End Phase" form an ability queue
and resolve.
• Abilities that occur "during the End Phase" form an ability queue and resolve.
• All circular tokens are removed from all ships (green, then orange).
• Each card with a recurring charge icon recovers that many charges. Each
card with a negative recurring charge icon loses that many charges.
After this phase, the criteria for winning the game are checked. If the game
did not end, the Planning Phase of the next round begins.

posts.author: Hansi
posts.text:
No, you can't keep the focus gained using Savage Oppress because his ability triggers during step 2 of the End Phase. This is how the chain is resolved:
• Overtune Modulators effect triggers at step 2 of the End Phase, the player establishes how many green token will be removed and the ship with Overtuned Modulators gets a matching amount of strain tokens.
• Savage Oppress triggers when strain tokens are assigned, replacing one strain with a focus.
• all green tokens, including the focus gained from Savage, are removed during step 3 of the End Phase.
• Save Oppress force charge is recovered during step 4 of the End Phase.

threads.title: SL Ronith Blario - "...if you are in the attackers firing arc..."

posts.text:
As Firing Arcs are defined in the RR as any arcs on the pilot card and any turret arcs.
If an enemy is attacking Rey with a HLC, and Ronith isnt in the bullseye for the HLC, but is in one of the enemy ships printed attack arcs, does Escort Fighter trigger?

posts.author: Hansi
posts.text: Yes, Escort Fighter can be triggered if Ronith Blario is inside any of the attacker's firing arcs, even if it's outside the arc used by the attack.

If a ship has two or more copies of the “Hull Breach” critical damage card and suffers further damage, does that damage trigger all Hull Breach cards simultaneously, or are the cards resolved one after another?
If they are triggered simultaneously, a single hit would result in as many critical effects as there are active Hull Breach cards. If the cards are resolved sequentially, however, it would only result in one critical effect, since the trigger condition for the additional Hull Breach cards would no longer apply.

posts.author: Hansi
posts.text: The two copies of Hull Breach are added together in the queue but they resolve separately. Hull Breach effect is a replacement effect and after the first copy is resolved, there are no more normal hits to be changed into critical hits so the second copy does not apply.
Iden’s ability (interceptor) says cancel a hit or crit. If there is a hit and a crit coming in, can Iden choose to cancel the crit? Or is does it just cancel the next damage (the hit)?

posts.author: Hansi
posts.text:
Step 5 of an Attack specifies:
"If the attack hits, the defender suffers damage for each uncanceled HIT and CRITICAL HIT result in the following order:
a. The defender suffers 1 HIT damage for each uncanceled HIT result. Then cancel all HIT results.
b. The defender suffers 1 CRITICAL HIT damage for each uncanceled CRITICAL HIT result. Then cancel all CRITICAL HIT results."
You can choose when to activate Iden's ability due the fact that every damage is a sub-step of step 5.

threads.title: Strain for Scum Maul’s Pilot Ability

cards.alt: Maul — Lord of the Shadow Collective

posts.text: With scum maul’s pilot ability, do both coordinated ships get a strain or only the 2nd ship ?

posts.author: Hansi
posts.text: Maul's ability specifies: "EACH friendly ship you coordinate this way gains 1 strain token." so both of them get a strain token.

During the System Phase, a ship deployed from a huge ship by executing a 5 speed straight maneuver. Later, during the Activation Phase, the huge ship performs a coordinate action. Th range of the coordinate is not modified by any other abilities, so it remains limited to range 1-2. Is the deployed ship a valid option, considering that it’s generally accepted that range 2 is equal to 5 base lengths, or a 5 speed straight maneuver (template)? Regardless of whether the ship deployed from the front or side of the huge ship, the smaller ship’s rear template guide nubs are certainly at range 2, but does the base itself need to be at (eclipsing) the edge of range 2 to be selectable?

posts.author: Hansi
posts.text:
Ship guide nubs are not valid to measure ranges, ranges must be checked to the target ship base.
Considering range 2 equal to a 5 straight template is not officially accepted, the only accepted method to measure ranges is using the range ruler contained the in X Wing core pack. This method must be used due the possibility of small manufacturing differences between official templates and rules, so you need to check with an official range rules to verify that the deployed ship is a valid option.
Third party components may be used but only if they match official components measures.
If the ship has one shield up going into its attack and uses determination, thus becoming not shielded in the middle of missing its attack, can it use fanatical for that attack?

posts.author: Hansi
posts.text:
RRG FAQs (Engagement Phase and Attacking section) state: "effects resolved during Step 2b: Modify Attack Dice and 3b: Modify Defense Dice do not use the ability queue, as they are resolved in the order described in that section of the rules reference."
So you can use Determination and sacrifice your last shield to add a focus result, then you can use Fanatical to modify that focus into hit result because the requirement is met when you activate the Talent.

How does random player order starting in round 2 work… is that still to break ties on IN for activation and shooting as normal? Or is that meant to have any IN ship if they ‘win’ to go first in player order that they will be first to move, last to shoot?

posts.author: Maui
posts.text: Player order is randomized and play proceeds normally, with ships activating and engaging according to their initiative, with player order breaking any ties.

Does Carnor Jax's ability require a ship to be at Range 0-1 AND in front arc, or Range 0-1 IN the front arc?
Syntax for Carnor Jax is "at range x, in arc y" whereas other abilities like Darth Vader crew and ISB Jingoist are "in y arc, at range x". There are other "at range x, and also in in arc y"-style abilities but they are written more clearly as separate statements.

posts.author: Hansi
posts.text: Carnor Jax's ability requires the enemy ship to be at Range 0-1 from Carnor and inside firing arc. The ability can trigger even if the enemy ship is at range 2 inside Carnor's firing arc but at range 0-1 from him.
Would a vulture/hyena take damage from an obstacle chosen by a seismic if they are range 0 of it with struts open?

posts.author: Hansi
posts.text: Yes, the Vulture/Hyena would take damage because it's the effect of the Seismic Charge detonating, it's not coming from the obstacle.
In the context on the original roll of dice, can you roll half the dice then the other half? Like if you’re rolling 5 dice, can you roll 3, then roll the other 2, before modding.

posts.author: Maui
posts.text: The player should roll the correct number of dice all at once, if possible. If there are not have enough dice available, the player should roll all the available dice, keep track of the results, and then roll again with as many as are needed to complete the roll.
What happens to a vulture/hyena on a rock with struts open and that rock is blown up by a seismic? What happens to the config and the next turns maneuver?

posts.author: Maui
posts.text:
Grappling/landing struts (open) state:
You ignore obstacles at range 0. You cannot perform [barrel roll] actions. After you reveal your dial, if you reveal a maneuver other than a [2 straight] and are at range 0 of an asteroid or debris cloud, skip your Execute Maneuver step and remove 1 stress token; if you revealed a right or left maneuver, rotate your ship 90° in that direction. After you execute a maneuver, flip this card.
When it is that ship's turn to activate, it reveals its dial and, because it is not at range 0 of an asteroid or debris cloud, it continues its activation normally, then flips the configuration to its Closed side at the end of its activation.

Can a ship preform the enemy overlap (bump) focus using an ability such as contraband cybernetics, Tycho, proud tradition, etc if it already has a stress token? To clarify, it didn’t do a blue move so keep a stress from the last turn.

posts.author: Maui
posts.text: No, a ship cannot perform the overlap focus action if it is stressed, even if it has an ability that allows it to perform actions while stressed. The rules require a ship to not be stressed in order to gain the opportunity to perform the action. The "perform actions while stressed" abilities do not overcome this rule.
Can scum Cad Bane pilot use his pilot ability to pass tokens to a remote? Assuming the attack hits, etc.

posts.author: Maui
posts.text: No, Cad Bane cannot use his ability to transfer a token to a defending remote. By rule, remotes cannot gain any tokens except for locks, and Cad Bane's ability cannot transfer a lock token.

threads.title: Republic Y-wing + Burst Laser Turret + Targeting Computer Ruling.

posts.text:
I have noticed an unfortunate rise in what looks like a familiar old 1.0 TLT list with the 7 Republic Y-wings equipped with a Burst Laser Turret and Targeting Computer. I will not get into the ugly feel of broken this list has with negative game play, but question on ruling-
The Republic Y-wing has the following built in ability – “Intuitive Interface: After you perform an action added to your action bar by a upgrade, you may perform a calculate action.” It appears players are adding a targeting computer upgrade in order to be able to target lock, then gain a calculate.
I would argue that since this ship already has a red target lock action, the Intuitive Interface would NOT trigger because you have not added the action, it is already on your action bar? Interested on a ruling here?
And side note, this list looks like good cause for looking into limiting non-unique pilots and also upgrade cards to avoid broken lists that no one enjoys flying against…

posts.author: Hansi
posts.text:
Second point under Actions in RRG specifically says:
"Some upgrade cards have an action bar that lists one or more actions. These actions are added to the ship’s action bar and therefore are standard actions that the ship can perform."
Therefore, Targeting Computer adds a white target lock action to the Resistance Y Wing action bar and it can be used in combination with Intuitive Interface.
For the rest of the question we suggest to report it under Feedback & Bugs section of the forum: https://www.xwing.life/forum/feedback
If klick uses his ability to cancel my r1 BLT, can I spend the second charge to add another dice?

posts.author: Hansi
posts.text:
Yes, you can do it but there is a difference depending on player order. Klick and BLT abilities trigger at step 2.a of the attack and:
if the defending player goes first, Klick resolves its ability and then the attacking player resolves BLT ability.
if the attacking player goes first, BLT ability has to be resolved before Klick and other abilities of the defending player.

threads.title: Dash (Freighter for Hire) and Ahsoka crew interactions with gas clouds.

posts.text:
If you activate the ability on Ahsoka's card but remain at range 0 of a gas cloud, is it still
possible to take a target lock action as part of your normal perform action step? If so, would Dash maintain the target lock going into the engagement phase?
In addition, what would happen if an enemy tried to lock Dash on a gas cloud?
Thanks in advance.

posts.author: Maui
posts.text:
Ahsoka Tano's ability causes the ship to ignore obstacles until the end of the Activation Phase. While Dash Rendar is ignoring obstacles, he can acquire locks and be locked even while at range 0 of a gas cloud.
Once the Activation phase ends and Ahsoka's ability is no longer in effect, Dash is at range 0 of the gas cloud and he can no longer acquire locks or be locked by other ships. This effect does not break any locks maintained by Dash, or any locks on Dash that are maintained by another ship.

threads.title: Vulture hitting a rock/debris after leaving a rock/debris

posts.text:
If a Vulture/Hyena leaves a rock/debris with a 2 straight and lands on another rock/debris, does it ignore the effects of overlapping since its struts are open at the time of overlap?
Similarly, what happens if the 2 straight is blocked and it lands on the same obstacle it tried to leave?

posts.author: Maui
posts.text:
A ship will ignore the effects of overlapping an obstacle while its Grappling/Landing Struts are in the Open position.
Grappling/Landing Struts (Open) read: "You ignore obstacles at range 0."
If the ship is physically on top of an obstacle, by rule it is also at range 0 of that obstacle, so any effects triggered by overlapping that obstacle during the maneuver are ignored.
Once all steps of executing the maneuver are complete, the Grappling/Landing Struts will flip to the Closed side, the ship is no longer ignoring the obstacle, and the ship is now subject to the effects of being at Range 0 of the obstacle (but not the effects of overlapping the obstacle).

Snap shot and targeting matrix
Opponent does a blue maneuver. Snap shot triggers.
I spend a focus result, giving a strain at the end of the neutralize results step.
Do they keep the strain? Or does it come off with the blue maneuver?

posts.author: Maui
posts.text:
Spending a result is considered a dice modification effect, so you cannot spend a result with Targeting Matrix while performing an attack with Snap Shot.
In the scenario where a bonus attack that does permit dice modification occurs "after a ship executes a maneuver," that attack would take place after the Check Difficulty step, so the defender could not immediately remove the strain from Targeting Matrix.

Intimidation says:
While an enemy ship at range 0 defends, it rolls 1 fewer defense die
Does this also include the r0 attack of the ship that has equipped the intimidation upgrade?

posts.author: Maui
posts.text:
No. A ship that is defending at attack range 0 cannot have its defense dice reduced by enemy ships.
Note that certain abilities (like Arvel Crynyd, RZ-1 A-wing) allow a ship to treat its attack range 0 primary attacks as though they are attack range 1, which would then permit the use of abilities like Outmaneuver.

Hello,
can a Vulture with open Grappling Struts be tractored away from an asteroid or debris cloud even if the maneuver template would overlap the obstacle while boosting or barrel-rolling?

posts.author: Maui
posts.text:
Grappling Struts (Open) instructs the ship to ignore obstacles at range 0. Since the ship is ignoring the obstacle, it can move through or overlap that obstacle while it boosts or barrel rolls, even if the template overlaps the obstacle.
This is the case even if the opposing player is the one moving the ship, similar to how the ship ability of the Starviper-class Attack Platform will cause that ship to use a 1 bank template when an opponent causes it to barrel roll after becoming tractored.
If an ioned ship forgets to assign a dial. Does it gain a stress and do the Stress Maneuver and retain its ion tokens? Or does it perform an ion maneuver; and if so, how is it resolved?

posts.author: Maui
posts.text: If an ionized ship forgets to assign a dial, that ship will gain a stress token and then execute a white 2 straight stress maneuver. Since it did not execute an ion maneuver, the ion tokens are not removed and the ship remains ionized.

Lando has Loose Stabilizer and does a blue bank, then adds his pilot ability to the queue first, and then Loose Stabilizer. He uses his ability to repair Loose Stabilizer. Does Loose Stabilizer still resolve now that it is no longer present?

posts.author: Hansi
posts.text: Yes, you can do that because Damage Cards with "Action:" are considered player's abilities and you can choose the order of resolution. In this case Loose Stabilizer does not resolve because it's not in play anymore.

With 'Targeting Matrix' equiped, while attack in Range 0:
a) can I spend 'focus' result - as it is not in '2.b Modify Attack Dice', but '4. Neutralize Results.'
or
b)it counts as Modify dice and is forbidden in R0?

posts.author: Maui
posts.text:
You cannot spend a result with Targeting Matrix while performing a primary attack at range 0.
Although the ability does not resolve during the Dice Modification step, it is still a dice modification effect that takes place during an attack, and the attacker is not permitted to modify the attack dice while performing a primary attack at range 0.
Note that this only applies to primary attacks; if you are performing a special attack at range 0 (for example, using the Hotshot Tail Blaster upgrade), you may modify the attack dice, including spending a result with Targeting Matrix.

threads.title: Coaxium Hyperfuel - timing of paying a cost

posts.text: When the second ability of Coaxium Hyperfuel is used, partially executing a maneuver and suffering a critical damage to perform a SLAM action, is the critical damage suffered before or after the SLAM action is performed (or rather at what point does the ability of a resulting damage card take effect)? The timing matters in cases of suffering critical damage that deals damage cards like Damaged Sensor Array, where the ability to SLAM might be fully interrupted, or Damaged Engine, where the difficulty of a potential turn option could be increased. The rules reference reads that costs can only be paid if the effect can be resolved, so the case of Damaged Sensor Array creates a bit of a conundrum. And the FAQ section further includes “The cost for an ability is paid when the ability is resolved,” and a ruling about the sequence of events when Pinpoint Tractor Array is used.

posts.author: Hansi
posts.text: Even if card wording may seem confusing, the FAQ regarding Pinpoint Tractor Array fully explain how to resolve the second ability of Coaxium Hyperfuel. When you resolve the ability to perform a slam, you suffer a critical hit or expose a damage card, but the effect from the damage card is added to the queue and applied once you completely resolve the slam action.

threads.title: Strut-Lock Override on Siege of Coruscant CIS pilots

posts.text:
Dear rules people,
Strut-Lock Override:
At the start of your activation, you may spend 1 (Charge). If you do, ignore obstacles while you move through them this round.
If you spend one of the charges from the Strut-Lock Override and then Maneuvre over an obstacle, so the maneuvre template overlaps at the rear of the ship but the base ends on top of the Obstacle.
During that ships action step, can you then barrel roll/boost off the obstacle as you ignore them while moving through them this turn?
Or does overlapping the obstacle trigger the effect of the obstacle? (I realise Overlapping and moving through are different things.)
Thanks

posts.author: Hansi
posts.text: Strut-Lock Override specifically says "move through", so the effect is limited to movements where the ship doesn't overlap the obstacle with its base. The effect applies also to barrel roll or boost actions.

Targeting Matrix: “While attacking, at the end of the Neutralize Results step, you may spend 1 focus result. If you do, after the attack is resolved, the defender gains 1 strain token.”
Can I spend a focus result before all results are cancelled by the tracers as the two effects seem to take place at the same time?

posts.author: Hansi
posts.text: You cannot use Targeting Matrix because dice results are cancelled before the End of Neutralize Results step. Once you find out that the attack hits, you activate Tracers effect to gain locks on the target and you must cancel all remaining dice results. You can activate Targeting Matrix only after that because it occurs at the End of that step, but there are no dice results left.
Does a ship that uses Pattern Analyzer to reposition off of an obstacle still skip its Perform Action Step?

posts.author: Maui
posts.text:
No, it will not skip its perform action step.
The effect of skipping your perform action step is triggered by ending your maneuver on an obstacle. Pattern Analyzer triggers while a ship is executing a red maneuver, meaning that the ship has not yet ended its maneuver, so using the action granted by Pattern Analyzer to reposition away from the obstacle will prevent you from suffering that effect. However, you will still suffer all the other effects of moving through or overlapping that obstacle.

threads.title: Parting Gift in the End of Activation

posts.text:
A ship with parting gift is destroyed by bombs at the end of activation. That ship drops a bomb using parting gift.
Does this new bomb detonate in that moment or at the next turns end of activation?

posts.author: Maui
posts.text:
The bomb will not detonate until the next round.
When you reach the end of activation, all 'at end of the activation phase' abilities are triggered and form a queue; this includes bomb detonation effects. This is the only opportunity for these abilities to enter the queue for the round. If a ship is destroyed by a bomb effect and then uses Parting Gift to drop an additional bomb, the 'at the end of the activation phase' opportunity has already passed, so the additional bomb's detonation ability will not be triggered until the end of the next round's activation phase.

"After you fully execute a red maneuver, you may coordinate a friendly ship at range 1-3."
Is this considered an action?

posts.author: Maui
posts.text: No; Hera's ability specifies that she may coordinate a friendly ship. This is different from performing a coordinate action, so she can do it while stressed and it does not count against her limit of 1 coordinate action per round.
